event_description: A user finished the guided first run (`hacklab setup`): scanned, signed in to Hacklab, answered the prompt-sharing question, and uploaded their usage. Props: tokens_total, rank (real rank when the upload returned one, else the anonymous preview), prompt_consent (none|stats|full).

How the end of `hacklab setup` handed off profile setup to a coding agent. Props: agent (the CLI binary found: claude|codex|grok; absent when none was), outcome — launched (the agent was started interactively), declined (an agent was offered and the user skipped it), unavailable (no agent CLI on PATH, or a non-TTY run), spawn_failed (the agent was found but would not start).
A user successfully authenticated via Hacklab device flow and a session was saved.
A user scanned local AI usage and generated a share card.
A user ran an interactive sync and their AI token usage was successfully uploaded.
The OS-native daily background sync was successfully installed. `source` says which command armed it: daemon (`hacklab daemon`), scan (`hacklab scan`), or setup (the guided first run).

The background sync could not be auto-scheduled (unsupported platform, or the scheduler write failed), so the manual cron instructions were printed instead. `source` says which command tried: daemon, scan, or setup.
A user ran `hacklab daemon off` and the OS-native daily background sync was torn down.
A user successfully posted a drop (short status update) to their profile.
A user published a new essay to their profile via the CLI.
A user updated an existing essay with new markdown content.
A user deleted an essay from their profile.
A user posted a message to the main community channel.
A user sent a direct message to another user.
A user published or refreshed a project on their profile via the CLI.
A user changed fields on an existing project via `hacklab project edit`.
A user deleted a project from their profile via the CLI.
A user logged out and their local session and daily sync were cleared.
A user saved profile fields (bio, links, open-to-work) via profile set, edit, or apply.
A user's referral link was surfaced via `hacklab referral` (via: cli for humans, json for agents; count = referrals joined, or null if the backend was unreachable).
